subject: Re: PayGrid model fit evaluation — next steps & parity thresholds
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: PayGrid model fit evaluation — next steps

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to understand PayGrid's fraud detection workflow and the latency constraints for batch scoring vs. realtime alerts. As promised, I wanted to summarize next steps and share the initial materials for the model fit evaluation.

Quick recap of action items we agreed on:
- PayGrid to share a small sample of anonymized examples (we discussed ~5k rows) and the target definition for fraud events.
- Redwood to run a 2-week evaluation comparing your current proprietary baseline against 3 open-model candidates with our standard prompt/feature set.
- We'll focus on: precision@k, false positive rate, response latency (p95), and cost per 1M tokens.

Attached you'll find:
- paygrid_eval_promptset_v1.txt — standard prompts + feature mapping we use for structured->text scoring.
- eval_instructions.md — how to run the harness locally if you prefer, or we can run it on Redwood Dedicated for you.
- benchmark_results_open_vs_proprietary.pdf — placeholder; we'll populate after first run.

Recommended initial model set (open candidates):
1) LlamaX-13B-Quant (8-bit) — good token efficiency, low cost.
2) Mistral-7B-Instruct — strong instruction-following with reasonable latency.
3) Redmond-13B-Opt (open variant) — closer architecture to your baseline; useful for parity checks.

Acceptance / parity discussion we touched on: as a stoplight, we'd expect open model parity within ≤10-15% relative drop in precision@k compared to your baseline for a green decision. Anything beyond 20% we'd call a fail in this short evaluation. We can refine thresholds per metric — happy to align.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the sample export timeline (EOD Wednesday would be ideal).
2) If you want us to run the eval on Redwood infrastructure, let us know and we’ll provision a Dedicated eval instance (we discussed cost estimate ~ $1.2k for the run).

Thanks — looping in Marissa on the technical side.

—
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Lauren — thanks for the detailed recap and the prompt set. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Sample export: we can provide the anonymized 5k rows by end of day Thursday (2026-03-04). Good?
2) Baseline: our proprietary model is an ensemble; for the eval please use the aggregated precision/recall numbers we sent in the data schema (I pasted again in the attached csv).
3) Parity thresholds: 10-15% relative drop sounds reasonable as a first bar, but can you confirm which metric you want to weight most? Our product team cares most about precision@10 and false positives (we tolerate some recall drop).

Also, curious on the open-model compute config you plan to run — could we get the cost breakdown and the expected p95 latency per model candidate?

Hi Samir / Lauren — looping in the engineering approach and some initial benchmarks.

Answering Samir's questions:
- Compute / config we plan to use (per candidate):
  * LlamaX-13B-Quant: 1x A10G, 8-bit quantized, expected p95 latency ~ 120ms for a 256-token scoring call; estimated cost for full eval run ≈ $950.
  * Mistral-7B-Instruct: 1x A10G, float16, p95 ~ 85ms; eval run cost ≈ $1,100 (higher due to throughput tuning).
  * Redmond-13B-Opt (open): 1x A100-40GB, mix-quant path, p95 ~ 140ms; eval run cost ≈ $1,250.

- Metric weighting proposal (we suggest):
  * Primary: precision@10 (weight 0.5)
  * Secondary: false positive rate (weight 0.3)
  * Tertiary: p95 latency (weight 0.2)

- Parity thresholds (recommended):
  * Green: <= 10% relative drop vs. proprietary baseline on weighted score
  * Amber: 10-20% relative drop (requires product review + additional prompt engineering)
  * Red: > 20% relative drop (not acceptable for go/no-go)

Attached is an initial benchmark template and the first-run prompt set (paygrid_eval_promptset_v1.txt). We'll run the evaluation on Redwood Dedicated unless PayGrid prefers to run locally. If we run it, we will provide the populated benchmark_results_open_vs_proprietary.pdf within 3 business days of receiving the sample.

Next steps for ops:
- Samir: confirm export timeline (Thu EOD) and whether you want Redwood to execute the run.
- Lauren: I can schedule the Dedicated instance and create a shared dashboard for the metrics.

—
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
